facts.statement: Credit risk arises when a borrower does not pay interest or instalments when due or on demand; it also arises on guarantees and letters of credit when funds are not forthcoming on crystallisation, in treasury products when payments from a counterparty cease, in trading when settlement fails, and in cross-border exposure when transfer of currency is restricted. Lending commands more than half of a bank's risk-taking, so management of credit risk is critical and is exercised across a large cross-section of branches. Credit risk management answers four questions (what are the risks; which, when and how much risk to accept; how to monitor and control; how to reduce it) through four parts: identification, measurement, monitoring and control, and mitigation.

Organisation for credit risk: the Board of Directors (overall responsibility; credit risk policies, procedures, aggregate limits, reporting and audit; decides the level of credit risk), the Risk Management Committee of the Board, the Credit Policy Committee or Credit Risk Management Committee (CPC or CRMC, which formulates policy on standards for credit proposals, financial covenants, rating standards, delegation of powers, limits on large exposures and asset concentrations, collateral standards, portfolio management, loan review, pricing and provisioning), and the Credit Risk Management Department (independent of credit administration, enforces and monitors compliance with risk parameters and prudential limits, develops risk assessment systems and MIS and undertakes loan review). Under the Reserve Bank's Credit Risk Management Directions, 2025 a bank puts in place a comprehensive Board approved policy on credit risk management covering related party lending, country risk, unhedged foreign currency exposure, valuation of properties and current, cash credit and overdraft accounts; follows the Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management; does its own independent and objective credit appraisal and does not depend on reports prepared by outside consultants, especially in-house consultants of the borrower; carries out sensitivity tests and scenario analysis for infrastructure projects (project delays and cost overruns); ascertains the source and quality of promoters' equity (debt of the parent must not be infused as equity of the subsidiary); and obtains credit information reports from one or more credit information companies.
facts.locator: Chapters II and III, paragraphs 5 to 11; S03 printed pp. 426-427, section 15.3

facts.statement: Credit risk has two components: default risk (failure to make promised payments, partly or wholly; the fraction normally paid is the recovery rate) and credit spread or downgrade risk (worsening credit quality widens the credit spread; reflected in rating downgrade and firm specific). Loans in the banking book are not marked to market, so default is the only credit event that causes immediate loss, while traded portfolios also face credit spread volatility. Default risk and downgrade risk are transaction level risks; portfolio risk has two components, systematic or intrinsic risk (the risk of the economy as a whole, reducible only by diversification across geographies, industries, borrowers and markets, to a minimum that corresponds to the economy's risk) and concentration risk (a portfolio with higher weight in one borrower, geography or industry). Counterparty risk is a variant arising from the trading partner's refusal or inability to perform, usually viewed as transient and linked to trading; country risk arises from restrictions imposed by a sovereign or from economic conditions. Under the Directions a bank must also have a Board approved country risk management policy within its credit risk management policy.
facts.locator: Printed pp. 427-429, sections 15.4; Directions Chapter VI, paragraph 44

facts.statement: Measurement of credit risk consists of credit rating or scoring and of estimating expected loan losses (the amount of loan losses a bank would expect over a chosen horizon, tracked over five or more years) and unexpected loan losses (the amount by which actual losses exceed expected losses, measured by the standard deviation of losses or the gap between expected losses and a chosen target quantile). Credit rating predicts whether the borrower will remain performing; it is built from financial, management, industry and business parameters. Because borrowers in a rating class behave consistently as a group, a bank can estimate defaults from its record: if 200 borrowers are rated A and 1 per cent have defaulted each year, about 2 are expected to default; if 400 are rated B and 5 per cent have defaulted, about 20 are expected to default. The expected cost of default is built into loan pricing so that lower-rated accounts are priced higher (risk-reward parity), and default probabilities by rating help assess the minimum capital required. Rating has nothing to do with profitability: it reflects stability of revenue generation.

A credit rating model needs data on defaults by rating category (rating migration). Rating migration is the change in a borrower's rating over time on the same model, usually studied for many accounts; in the courseware's illustration of 100 accounts rated A, after a year 1 was A++, 1 A+, 79 stayed A, 10 became B++, 4 B+, 3 B and 2 defaulted, implying a 2 per cent default probability for that class. A bank's model is tested on whether it covers the standard rating factors (management, financials, conduct, business and industry) and whether its migration maps fairly to the pattern published by accredited agencies; if the bank shows 2 per cent default for A while agencies show 0.2 per cent, the model would be mapped to a lower grade. Models named in the courseware: the Altman Z score (a combination of five financial ratios forecasting bankruptcy within 12 months), J.P. Morgan's CreditMetrics (volatility of asset values from rating migration; for economic capital under a RAROC framework) and Credit Suisse's CreditRisk+ (an actuarial method for expected default rates and unexpected losses, from which conditional VaR or expected shortfall can be computed; banks using it for capital calculation do so under the advanced IRB approach with supervisory approval). Banks should have a comprehensive risk scoring system (retail) or credit rating system (large loans) that is structured and periodically reviewed.

Credit risk control rests on a comprehensive management information system and credit information system. At transaction level the instruments are the credit appraisal process, risk analysis process, credit audit and loan review mechanism and monitoring process, with standards in the Board approved loan policy for delegation of powers, credit appraisal, rating standards and benchmarks, pricing strategy and loan review. Credit approving authority: a delegation of powers scheme and a multi-tier system in which proposals above a limit are approved by an approval grid or committee of at least 3 or 4 officers, invariably including one officer from the Credit Risk Management Department who has no volume or profit targets; no proposal is approved against the majority view of the grid, and dissent is recorded. Credit appraisal guidelines include borrower standards, procedures, covenants, rating standards and pricing. Prudential limits may cover financial and profitability ratios, credit exposure, asset concentration, large exposures and the maturity profile of the loan book, with deviations approved by named authorities. Credit ratings are reviewed at least half-yearly (quarterly updating preferred) and an independent loan review group verifies them; a migration study is done periodically. Risk pricing: pricing should be risk based, with the credit spread reflecting expected loss and charges on capital, linked to the probability of default and so to the rating, with collateral, relationship and strategic reasons also entering; price cutting for market share distorts risk-reward parity.

At portfolio level, credit control tracks risk of a given portfolio, expected losses, risk capital, concentration effects and diversification benefits. Activities: identifying portfolio weakness in advance through credit quality migrations; moving from obligor-specific risk to concentration effects; stipulating quantitative ceilings on exposure by rating category and industry; and, once banks migrate to the foundation and advanced IRB approaches with the Reserve Bank's approval, using credit portfolio value at risk models. Tracking non-performing loans around the balance sheet date does not signal the quality of the whole loan book; tracking migration at quarterly or half-yearly intervals does. Measures include ceilings on aggregate exposure by rating, rating-wise distribution of borrowers by industry, industry and sector monitoring (raising quality standards for a badly performing industry), targets for probable defaults and provisioning, rapid portfolio reviews, stress tests and scenario analysis, and discriminatory review schedules. External factors (economy, commodity prices, exchange and interest rates, restrictions, policies) and internal factors (loan policy and administration deficiencies, absence of concentration limits, weak appraisal, excessive dependence on collateral, inadequate risk-pricing, no loan review or post-sanction surveillance) drive portfolio credit risk. Active portfolio management responds to disintermediation, capital mobility, lower returns, and to new products (pass through certificates, syndicated lending, structured finance) and new tools (secondary loan trading, securitisation, credit derivatives).

The Loan Review Mechanism (credit audit) evaluates the quality of the loan book and credit administration. Its objectives: promptly identify loans developing weaknesses and start corrective action; evaluate portfolio quality and isolate problem areas; provide information for deciding the adequacy of loan loss provisions; assess adherence to loan policies and procedures and legal compliance; and give top management information on credit administration. Accurate and timely credit grading is a basic component, and ratings given by the risk management or credit administration department are reviewed by Loan Review Officers independent of loan administration, who report to the Board or a Board committee. Reviews of high value loans are usually within three months of sanction or renewal, or sooner when deterioration is indicated; all loans above a cut-off should be reviewed and at least 30 to 40 per cent of the portfolio should be subjected to review in a year. Depth covers approval, accuracy and timeliness of ratings, adherence to policy and law, covenants, post-sanction follow-up, documentation, portfolio quality and recommendations; the quality of credit decisions is evaluated within about 3 to 6 months. Small value retail loans are reviewed on an exception or sample basis.

Credit risk mitigation at transaction level uses traditional techniques (first priority claims on cash, securities or landed property; third party guarantees) and recent ones (a credit derivative); at portfolio level, securitisation and credit derivatives help to diversify and shape the portfolio. CRM reduces or transfers credit risk but may increase legal, operational, liquidity and market risks, so the advantages must be weighed against the risks acquired. Capital treatment is taught in unit 3.

Securitisation converts illiquid loans into tradable securities through a special purpose vehicle (SPV or SPE), which issues securities (pass-through certificates) serviced from the cash flows of the pool; the originating bank transfers the assets and the credit risk to investors. A traditional securitisation uses the cash flow of an underlying pool to service at least two stratified risk positions (tranches); a synthetic securitisation transfers credit risk of a pool, in whole or part, through funded (credit linked notes) or unfunded (credit default swaps or guarantees) means. Under the Reserve Bank's Securitisation Directions, 2025, the minimum retention requirement (MRR) ensures the originator has a continuing stake: 5 per cent of the book value of the loans for underlying loans with original maturity of 24 months or less, and 10 per cent for original maturity of more than 24 months and for loans with bullet repayments (other than residential mortgage backed securities); for residential mortgage backed securities 5 per cent irrespective of maturity. Up to 5 per cent it is retained as first loss facility, then equity tranche, then pari passu in the remaining tranches sold; above 5 per cent in any combination of first loss, equity or other tranches sold to investors; over-collateralisation is not counted as first loss; investment in an interest only strip does not count; and the MRR cannot be reduced through hedging of credit risk or selling. A clean-up call is an option for the originator to call the exposures when the outstanding value falls below a pre-defined threshold; a credit enhancement is a contractual arrangement mitigating credit risk of a securitisation exposure and gives added protection to other parties; first loss facility is the first level of financial support. A collateralised loan obligation is a securitised pool of commercial loans with tranches serviced in order of seniority and unlike a credit linked note it covers a diverse pool.
facts.locator: Paragraphs 4, 11 to 15; S03 printed pp. 440-442, section 15.12

facts.statement: A credit derivative is an over-the-counter contract that transfers the credit risk of an asset or portfolio, usually without transferring the asset from the originator's books; the protection buyer pays periodic premiums to the protection seller, and on a credit event the seller compensates the buyer, by physical settlement (the buyer delivers a deliverable obligation against the notional amount) or cash settlement (the seller pays the notional amount less the expected recovery value). The courseware, following ISDA, lists six credit events: bankruptcy, obligation acceleration, obligation default, failure to pay, repudiation or moratorium and restructuring. Forms: credit default swaps (the buyer pays a premium for protection against a credit event on a reference obligation), total return swaps (the total return payer transfers the entire economic performance of a reference asset to the receiver for a pre-determined fixed or floating rate; the formula in the courseware is interest flows plus final value minus original value of the underlying), credit linked notes (an on-balance sheet debt instrument with an embedded credit derivative; a securitised form of a credit default swap) and credit spread options (protection against widening of spread). Motives of buyers: transfer credit risk without selling the asset, hedging, regulatory capital relief, diversification; of sellers: yield, speculation, arbitrage, diversification. The Reserve Bank's Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026, in force from 25 June 2026 (superseding the 2022 Directions the courseware describes), cover credit default swaps, total return swaps, exchange traded credit derivatives and futures on credit indices; market-makers are scheduled commercial banks (other than small finance, payment, local area and regional rural banks), standalone primary dealers, upper and middle layer NBFCs and EXIM Bank, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI and NaBFID; users are retail or non-retail; at least one party must be a market-maker or an authorised central counterparty; OTC trades are reported to the CCIL trade repository within 30 minutes.
facts.locator: Paragraphs 1 to 4 and 4.5.5; S03 printed pp. 442-448, section 15.13

payload.title: Where credit risk comes from and how it is managed
The credit risk organisation and the Reserve Bank's policy requirements
The kinds of credit risk
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Two components**: **default risk** (**failure to pay**; the share paid is the **recovery rate**) and **credit spread / downgrade risk** (**worse quality widens the spread**; firm specific).

Loans in the banking book are **not marked to market**, so **default is the only event that causes immediate loss**; traded portfolios also face **spread volatility**.

| Level | Risk | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Transaction** | **default**, **downgrade** | one borrower |
| **Portfolio** | **systematic (intrinsic)** | **the economy's risk**; **cut only by diversification** |
| | **concentration** | **too much in one borrower, area or industry** |
| **Related** | **counterparty** | **trading partner fails to perform**; transient |
| | **country** | **restrictions imposed by a country**, or its economy |

A bank must also have a **Board approved country risk policy** inside its credit risk policy.

payload.title: Credit rating, expected loss and pricing
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Measurement** = **rating or scoring** + **estimate of losses**:
- **Expected loss**: losses **normally expected** over a horizon (tracked **five or more years**).
- **Unexpected loss**: **actual losses above expected**, measured by **standard deviation of losses** or the gap to a **target quantile**.

**Rating** predicts whether the borrower **stays performing**. Inputs: **financial, management, industry and business parameters**. It reflects **stability of revenue**, **not profitability**.

**From rating to price**: a class behaves **consistently** as a group. If **200 borrowers rated A** have shown **1%** default a year, expect **2** to default; if **400 rated B** show **5%**, expect **20**. That **cost of default goes into the loan price**, so **lower-rated accounts cost more** (**risk-reward parity**). Default rates by rating also help set **minimum capital**.

payload.title: Rating migration and credit risk models
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Rating migration** = the **change in a borrower's rating over time** on the **same model**. It is studied **across many accounts**.

**Illustration (courseware)**: **100 accounts rated A** a year ago: **1 A++, 1 A+, 79 A, 10 B++, 4 B+, 3 B, 2 default**, so a **2% default rate** for that class.

**Testing a bank's model**: does it cover the **standard rating factors** and does its **migration map to the pattern published by accredited agencies**? If the bank shows **2%** where agencies show **0.2%** for a grade, the bank's model is **mapped to a lower grade**.

| Model | Idea |
| --- | --- |
| **Altman Z score** | **five financial ratios** forecast **bankruptcy within 12 months** |
| **CreditMetrics** (J.P. Morgan) | **volatility of asset values from rating migration**; used for **economic capital** |
| **CreditRisk+** (Credit Suisse) | **actuarial** method for **expected defaults and unexpected losses**; yields **conditional VaR / expected shortfall**; capital use needs **supervisory approval** under **advanced IRB** |

payload.title: Controlling credit risk at the transaction level
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Instruments**: **appraisal, risk analysis, credit audit and loan review, monitoring**, backed by an **MIS and credit information system**.

**Approval**: **delegation of powers**; larger proposals go to an **approval grid** of **at least 3 or 4 officers**, **always including one from the Credit Risk Management Department (no volume or profit targets)**. **No approval against the majority**; **dissent is recorded**.

**Prudential limits** may cover **financial ratios, credit exposure, asset concentration, large exposures, maturity profile**; **deviations need named authority**.

**Ratings**: reviewed **at least half-yearly** (**quarterly preferred**), verified by an **independent loan review group**, with a **migration study**.

**Risk pricing**: **risk-based**, the spread reflecting **expected loss and the capital charge**; **collateral, relationship and strategic value** can modify it, but **price cutting for share breaks risk-reward parity**.

payload.title: Credit control at the portfolio level and active portfolio management
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Portfolio view**: **expected loss, risk capital, concentration, diversification**.

**Activities**: spot weakness **early through migration**; look at **concentration**, not just single obligors; set **ceilings by rating category and industry**; later, **credit portfolio VaR models** once banks adopt **FIRB/AIRB with RBI approval**.

**Why migration beats NPA tracking**: counting **NPAs around the balance sheet date** does not show **the quality of the whole book**; **quarterly or half-yearly migration** does.

**Portfolio quality measures**: **rating-wise ceilings**, **industry distribution**, **higher standards for a badly performing industry**, **targets for defaults and provisions**, **rapid reviews, stress tests, scenarios**.

**Drivers**: **external** (economy, commodity prices, exchange and interest rates, restrictions, policy) and **internal** (weak policy, **no concentration limits**, **poor appraisal**, **collateral dependence**, **bad pricing**, **no loan review**).

**Active portfolio management** responds to **disintermediation, capital mobility, lower returns** and uses **secondary loan trading, securitisation, credit derivatives**.

payload.title: The loan review mechanism
payload.core_explanation_md:
**LRM** (credit audit) tests **loan quality and credit administration**.

**Objectives**: **spot weak loans early and act**; **evaluate portfolio quality**; **inform loan loss provisioning**; **check policy and legal compliance**; **inform top management**.

- **Independence**: **loan review officers are independent of loan administration** and report to the **Board or a Board committee**; they **review the ratings** given by risk or credit administration.
- **Frequency**: **high value loans within about three months of sanction or renewal** (sooner if trouble signs); **every loan over a set cut-off**; and **30–40% or more of the portfolio each year**.
- **Depth**: **approval, rating accuracy and timeliness, policy and law, covenants, post-sanction follow-up, documentation, portfolio quality**; quality of **credit decisions judged within 3–6 months**.
- **Small retail loans**: **by exception or sample**.

payload.title: Securitisation and the minimum retention requirement
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Securitisation**: **illiquid loans become tradable securities** (**pass-through certificates**) issued by an **SPV/SPE**, serviced from the **pool's cash flows**; the **originator transfers assets and credit risk**.
- **Traditional**: pool cash flows service **at least two tranches**.
- **Synthetic**: **risk transferred by funded (credit linked notes) or unfunded (CDS, guarantees)** means.

**Minimum retention requirement (MRR) under the 2025 Directions**
| Underlying loans | MRR |
| --- | --- |
| **Original maturity ≤ 24 months** | **5% of book value** |
| **> 24 months, and bullet loans** | **10%** |
| **Residential mortgage backed securities** | **5%**, whatever the maturity |

**How it is held**: **up to 5%**: **first loss facility**, then **equity tranche**, then **pari passu in the other tranches sold**; **above 5%**: **any mix** of first loss, equity or other tranches. **Over-collateralisation is not first loss**; **interest only strips do not count**; **MRR cannot be hedged or sold**.

**Terms**: **clean-up call** (originator may call the pool when it falls **below a threshold**); **credit enhancement** (**added protection** to other parties); **first loss facility** (**first level of support**); **CLO** = **securitised pool of commercial loans**, **tranches paid by seniority**, **diverse pool** unlike a credit linked note.

payload.title: Credit derivatives: contracts and settlement
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Credit derivative**: an **OTC contract transferring credit risk without moving the asset**. **Protection buyer** pays **premium**; **protection seller** pays on a **credit event**.

**Settlement**
- **Physical**: the buyer **delivers a deliverable obligation** and receives the **notional amount**.
- **Cash**: the seller pays **notional less the expected recovery value**.

**ISDA credit events (courseware)**: **bankruptcy, obligation acceleration, obligation default, failure to pay, repudiation/moratorium, restructuring**.

| Form | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Credit default swap** | buyer pays **premium** for **protection against a credit event** on a **reference obligation** |
| **Total return swap** | payer passes **the entire economic performance** of an asset (interest plus **price change**) for a **fixed or floating rate**; covers **market risk too** |
| **Credit linked note** | **on-balance sheet** debt instrument with an **embedded credit derivative** (**a securitised CDS**) |
| **Credit spread option** | protects against **widening of the spread** |

**Buyers want**: **risk transfer without selling, hedging, capital relief, diversification**. **Sellers want**: **yield, speculation, arbitrage, diversification**.

payload.title: The Reserve Bank's Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026
payload.core_explanation_md:
**In force from 25 June 2026**; they **replace the 2022 Directions** (the courseware describes the **2022** framework).

- **Scope**: **credit default swaps, total return swaps, exchange traded credit derivatives and futures on credit indices**.
- **Market-makers**: **scheduled commercial banks** (not **small finance, payment, local area or regional rural banks**), **standalone primary dealers**, **upper and middle layer NBFCs**, and **EXIM Bank, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI, NaBFID**.
- **Users**: **retail or non-retail**.
- **One party at least** must be a **market-maker or an authorised central counterparty**.
- **Reporting**: **OTC trades to the CCIL trade repository within 30 minutes**.

**Examples of use**: **hedge a loan concentration** by a **total return swap** with an investor; **lay off the excess of a large commitment** by a **CDS bought from another bank**; **buy protection from a lowly correlated counterparty to diversify**; **put a price floor under an illiquid bond** with a total return swap.

payload.title: Expected defaults and the risk premium for a rating class
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank has 500 borrowers rated A, with a historical default rate of 0.8% a year, and 300 rated B with a default rate of 4% a year. Average loan is ₹50 lakh and loss given default is 60%. Find the expected defaults in each class and the expected loss per year as a percentage of the class's outstanding amount.

worked_steps.description: Expected loss on class B in rupees.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Expected defaults are 4 (A) and 12 (B); the expected loss is 0.48% and 2.40% of outstanding, which is the minimum risk premium for each class

self_check.prompt_text: Why must class B be priced above class A?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Its higher expected loss has to be recovered in the price (risk-reward parity), otherwise the bank earns less than its cost of risk.

payload.title: Reading a rating migration table
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: of 200 accounts rated B at the start of the year, after a year 4 are rated A, 130 remain B, 40 have moved to C, 18 to D and 8 have defaulted. Find the probabilities of staying, upgrade, downgrade and default.
payload.final_answer_with_unit: A B-rated account has a 65% chance of staying, 2% of upgrade, 29% of downgrade and 4% of default

self_check.prompt_text: What does a 4% default rate for this class tell the bank?
self_check.expected_takeaway: It is the class's default probability for pricing and capital, to be compared with the pattern published by accredited agencies.

payload.title: Minimum retention on a securitised pool
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank securitises (i) a pool of auto loans of original maturity 18 months and book value ₹300 crore, (ii) a pool of term loans of original maturity 60 months and book value ₹500 crore, and (iii) a residential mortgage pool of book value ₹400 crore with 20-year maturity. Find the minimum retention for each pool.
payload.final_answer_with_unit: The minimum retention is ₹15 crore, ₹50 crore and ₹20 crore respectively

self_check.prompt_text: May the bank hedge part of the retained ₹50 crore to reduce its risk?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The MRR may not be reduced through hedging of credit risk or selling.

payload.title: Cash settlement of a credit default swap
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: a bank buys three-year protection on a ₹60 crore bond at a premium of 1.5% a year, paid annually. A credit event occurs after exactly two years, and the bond's expected recovery value is 40% of the notional. Find the premiums paid and the cash settlement received.
payload.final_answer_with_unit: The bank paid ₹1.8 crore of premium and receives ₹36 crore (notional less expected recovery)

self_check.prompt_text: What would the premium outflow have been if no credit event had occurred?
self_check.expected_takeaway: ₹0.9 crore a year for the full three years, ₹2.7 crore, with no payment from the seller.

payload.stem_md: What do ratings measure, according to the courseware?

options.explanation_md: Profit margin is not what a rating measures.
Borrower size is not what a rating measures.
The age of the firm is not what a rating measures.

options.text_md: Stability of revenue generation, not profitability
options.explanation_md: Ratings measure the stability of revenue generation, not profitability.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Ratings measure the stability of revenue generation, not profitability.

payload.stem_md: What is an unexpected loan loss?

options.text_md: The amount by which actual losses exceed expected losses
options.explanation_md: Unexpected loss is the amount by which actual losses exceed expected losses.
The loss expected every year is expected loss.
Recovery through guarantees is a mitigant.

options.text_md: A loss on a trading position
options.explanation_md: A trading loss is market risk.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Unexpected loss is the amount by which actual losses exceed expected losses.

payload.stem_md: What does rating migration mean?

options.text_md: Moving a loan to another bank
options.explanation_md: Moving a loan to another bank is a transfer.

options.text_md: The change in a borrower's rating over a period when rated on the same model
options.explanation_md: Rating migration is the change in a borrower's rating over a period on the same model.

options.text_md: A change in the rating agency
options.explanation_md: A change of agency is not migration.

options.text_md: The transfer of a loan to NPA
options.explanation_md: Transfer to NPA is a downgrade to default, not migration as defined.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Rating migration is the change in a borrower's rating over a period on the same model.

payload.stem_md: A bank's model shows a 2 per cent default rate for its A rated borrowers while rating agencies show 0.2 per cent for A. What follows?

options.explanation_md: Something does follow from the gap.
The model is not rated higher; it understates risk sensitivity.

options.text_md: The bank's model is mapped to a lower grade, as it does not capture risk sensitivity in line with agency standards
options.explanation_md: A 2 per cent default rate against 0.2 per cent for agencies means the bank's model is mapped to a lower grade.
The agencies' pattern is not rejected.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A 2 per cent default rate against 0.2 per cent for agencies means the bank's model is mapped to a lower grade.

payload.stem_md: Which model forecasts the probability of bankruptcy within 12 months using five financial ratios?

options.explanation_md: CreditMetrics is a portfolio value at risk model.
CreditRisk+ is an actuarial default model.
RAROC measures risk adjusted return.
The Altman Z score predicts bankruptcy within 12 months using five financial ratios.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The Altman Z score predicts bankruptcy within 12 months using five financial ratios.

payload.stem_md: What is the minimum composition of the credit approval grid for larger proposals in the courseware?

options.text_md: At least 3 or 4 officers, including one from the Credit Risk Management Department
options.explanation_md: The approval grid has at least three or four officers including one from the Credit Risk Management Department.
One officer is not a grid.
Two branch officers lack independence.
The Chairman alone is not a grid.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The approval grid has at least three or four officers including one from the Credit Risk Management Department.

payload.stem_md: What should happen if a majority of the approval grid does not agree on the creditworthiness of the borrower?

options.explanation_md: The Chairman cannot override a failed grid.

options.text_md: The proposal is not approved or recommended to higher authorities, and dissent is recorded
options.explanation_md: If most of the grid disagrees, the proposal is not approved or recommended, and dissent is recorded.
Automatic approval would defeat the grid.
The borrower is not rated higher to fix disagreement.

payload.correct_explanation_md: If most of the grid disagrees, the proposal is not approved or recommended, and dissent is recorded.

payload.stem_md: How often should credit ratings be reviewed and updated at the least?

options.explanation_md: Five years is far too long.
Review only at renewal is too infrequent.
Ratings are reviewed at least half-yearly, with quarterly preferred.
Review is required, so never is wrong.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Ratings are reviewed at least half-yearly, with quarterly preferred.

payload.stem_md: Why is tracking migration of ratings better than tracking non-performing loans around the balance sheet date?

options.explanation_md: NPAs are recorded and reported.
Cheapness is not the reason.

options.text_md: Because the Reserve Bank forbids NPA tracking
options.explanation_md: The Reserve Bank does not forbid tracking NPAs.

options.text_md: Because NPAs at a date do not signal the quality of the entire loan book, while migration shows weaknesses in advance
options.explanation_md: NPAs at a single date do not show the quality of the whole book, while migration warns of weakness in advance.

payload.correct_explanation_md: NPAs at a single date do not show the quality of the whole book, while migration warns of weakness in advance.

payload.stem_md: Which is an internal factor driving portfolio credit risk?

options.explanation_md: Excessive dependence on collateral is a bank-side factor, so it is internal.
Changes in monetary policy are external.
Economic sanctions are external.
Commodity price swings are external.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Excessive dependence on collateral is a bank-side factor, so it is internal.

payload.stem_md: What proportion of the loan portfolio should at least be subjected to loan review in a year?

options.explanation_md: Five per cent is too small a sample.
At least 30 to 40 per cent of the portfolio should be reviewed each year.
A full review each year is beyond the stated minimum.
Some review is required.

payload.correct_explanation_md: At least 30 to 40 per cent of the portfolio should be reviewed each year.

payload.stem_md: To whom should loan review officers report their findings?

options.explanation_md: Loan administration is the function being reviewed.
The borrower cannot receive review findings.

options.text_md: Directly to the Board or a Committee of the Board
options.explanation_md: Loan review officers report directly to the Board or a Board Committee to keep them independent.
The dealing room has no role in credit review.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Loan review officers report directly to the Board or a Board Committee to keep them independent.

payload.stem_md: How soon after sanction or renewal are reviews of high value loans usually undertaken?

options.explanation_md: Three years is far too late.
Review after closure is pointless.
Waiting for default defeats early warning.
High value loans are usually reviewed within three months of sanction or renewal.

payload.correct_explanation_md: High value loans are usually reviewed within three months of sanction or renewal.

payload.stem_md: What is a risk of using credit risk mitigation techniques, according to the courseware?

options.text_md: They may increase legal, operational, liquidity and market risks
options.explanation_md: Mitigation techniques may add legal, operational, liquidity and market risks.
They do not always remove all risk.
They do not reduce capital to zero.
They carry costs and new risks.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Mitigation techniques may add legal, operational, liquidity and market risks.

payload.stem_md: What is the minimum retention requirement for a securitisation of loans with an original maturity of 36 months (other than residential mortgages)?

options.explanation_md: Five per cent is below the stated minimum.

options.text_md: 10 per cent of the book value
options.explanation_md: For such a securitisation the minimum retention is 10 per cent of the book value.
Fifteen per cent is above the stated minimum.
Zero would remove the originator's stake.

payload.correct_explanation_md: For such a securitisation the minimum retention is 10 per cent of the book value.

payload.stem_md: Which of the following counts towards the minimum retention requirement?

options.text_md: Investment in the interest only strip
options.explanation_md: Investment in the interest only strip does not count.
Over-collateralisation as first loss does not count.

options.text_md: A first loss facility provided by the originator
options.explanation_md: A first loss facility by the originator counts towards the minimum retention.
A hedged retained tranche does not count.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A first loss facility by the originator counts towards the minimum retention.

payload.stem_md: What is a clean-up call?

options.explanation_md: A call for more margin is a margin call.

options.text_md: A call on the investor to pay
options.explanation_md: A call on the investor to pay is a capital call.
A call option on shares is an equity instrument.

options.text_md: An option for the originator to call the exposures when the outstanding value falls below a pre-defined threshold
options.explanation_md: A clean-up call lets the originator call the exposures when the outstanding value falls below a pre-defined level.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A clean-up call lets the originator call the exposures when the outstanding value falls below a pre-defined level.

payload.stem_md: On a credit event, how does cash settlement of a credit default swap work?

options.text_md: The protection seller pays the notional amount less the expected recovery value
options.explanation_md: In cash settlement the protection seller pays the notional less the expected recovery value.

options.text_md: The buyer pays the premium again
options.explanation_md: The buyer paying the premium again is not settlement.

options.text_md: The buyer delivers the reference obligation
options.explanation_md: Delivery of the obligation is physical settlement.
Something is paid on a credit event.

payload.correct_explanation_md: In cash settlement the protection seller pays the notional less the expected recovery value.

payload.stem_md: Which instrument is an on-balance sheet equivalent of a credit default swap?

options.explanation_md: A total return swap is a different off-balance sheet derivative.
A credit linked note is the on-balance sheet equivalent of a credit default swap.
A credit spread option is a different derivative.
A guarantee is not a derivative equivalent.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A credit linked note is the on-balance sheet equivalent of a credit default swap.

payload.stem_md: How does a total return swap differ from a credit default swap?

options.explanation_md: It does not cover only default.
It involves payments of return.

options.text_md: It transfers the total economic return of the asset, including market risk, not only credit risk
options.explanation_md: A total return swap transfers the asset's whole economic return, including market risk, not just credit risk.

options.text_md: It is issued on exchanges only
options.explanation_md: It is not limited to exchanges.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A total return swap transfers the asset's whole economic return, including market risk, not just credit risk.

payload.stem_md: From when are the Reserve Bank's Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026 in force?

options.explanation_md: 10 February 2022 is not the stated date.
1 April 2026 is not the stated date.
1 October 2026 is not the stated date.
The Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026 are in force from 25 June 2026.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026 are in force from 25 June 2026.

payload.stem_md: Within what time must market-makers report OTC credit derivative transactions to the CCIL trade repository?

options.explanation_md: Market-makers must report OTC credit derivative trades to the CCIL repository within 30 minutes.
One day is longer than allowed.
A week is far longer than allowed.
Month end is far longer than allowed.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Market-makers must report OTC credit derivative trades to the CCIL repository within 30 minutes.

payload.stem_md: A bank has 250 borrowers rated A with a historical default rate of 1.2% a year. How many defaults does it expect in a year, to one decimal?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 1 decimal places.

payload.stem_md: A bank securitises term loans of original maturity 48 months, book value ₹720 crore. What is the minimum retention, in ₹ crore?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Original maturity over 24 months: MRR is 10%; 10% of 720 = 72.

payload.stem_md: A bank buys protection on a ₹80 crore bond. A credit event occurs and the expected recovery value is 35% of the notional. What cash settlement does the bank receive, in ₹ crore?
payload.correct_explanation_md: Recovery = 80 × 35% = 28; settlement = 80 − 28 = ₹52 crore.

payload.stem_md: A bank's loan book is ₹12,000 crore. The least it should subject to loan review in a year is 30% of the portfolio. How much is that, in ₹ crore?

In a total return swap the payer passes the interest flows plus the change in value of the reference asset. Interest flows over the period are ₹6.4 crore, the original value of the asset was ₹100 crore and the final value ₹96.5 crore. What is the amount the payer passes on, in ₹ crore, to one decimal?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 1 decimal places.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Total return = interest flows + (final − original) = 6.4 + (96.5 − 100) = 6.4 − 3.5 = 2.9.

payload.stem_md: Of 250 accounts rated B, 175 stay B, 10 are upgraded, 55 are downgraded and the rest default. What is the default rate, in per cent?

unresolved: The Reserve Bank's Credit Risk Management Directions copy used is updated to 1 October 2026 and includes amendments dated January, April and July 2026; the chapters used (II, III, VI) were taken from the copy without separating amendments that took effect after the 30 June 2026 cut-off. The Guidance Note on Credit Risk Management (the courseware's source for much of sections 15.4 to 15.10) was not read.

Credit derivatives: the courseware describes the 2022 Directions (market-maker net owned funds of ₹500 crore, single-name CDS only, reference obligations limited to money market instruments and rated INR corporate bonds). Those Directions were superseded by the Credit Derivatives Directions, 2026 on 25 June 2026, five days before the cut-off. The 2026 text was read only through a website reproduction (not the Reserve Bank's file); the items teach the 2026 framework at the level of scope, participants, definitions and reporting and do not test the 2022 thresholds.

The courseware's illustrations (100 accounts rated A migrating over 31.3.2016 to 31.3.2017, the sponge iron plant and oil company examples, the Greek debt crisis) are not reproduced; all figures here are new. The courseware's statement that the Reserve Bank directed ratings of borrowers is not tested.
CreditMetrics, CreditRisk+ and the Altman Z score are described only as the courseware does; no source was read for them. ISDA credit events are the courseware's list.
The courseware cites an MRR Master Direction dated 24 September 2021; the 2025 Securitisation Directions were read for the retention figures (they agree) and the courseware's 2021 date is not used.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
